trigger: Build a config_only runtime package for an AI node — no custom binary, only package.json and ai.generic's default config.
constraints: package.json must include: name (lowercase, dots/hyphens allowed), version (semver), type, runtime_base
runtime_base must match one of the available runtimes in known_context.available_runtimes

config/default-config.json must be valid JSON: ai.generic's config, behavior.kind ai_chat; it names a provider or a model only when the agent needs its own (the hive's otherwise), and a model always of the node's provider
the package carries no prompt: an agent's prompt is its ILK definition (role, skills, handbooks)
name in package.json must be lowercase with no spaces
do_not_repeat: do not use 'full_runtime' as type for config_only packages — use 'config_only'
do not invent a runtime_base that is not in the known available runtimes
do not omit package.json or config/default-config.json — both are required
do not include binary files or executables in inline_package artifacts
do not add prompt files or instructions: ai.generic refuses instructions in its config

trigger: Build the workflow definition a wf_deployment carries.

definition.description: A person talks with AI.sales: each of their messages goes to sales with a menu, and sales' answer goes back to them. The conversation closes when the person stops writing.

states.name: start
states.description: Hands the person's first message to sales.

states.name: talking
states.description: Each message of the person goes to sales with its menu, and the catch gives the person sales' answers. Each message starts the quiet time again.

content.default: Sorry, something went wrong on our side. Could you write that again?

constraints: the artifact is what a wf_deployment carries: workflow_name and definition
workflow_name is lowercase letters, digits and '-' in dot-separated parts, each starting with a letter, and matches the wf_deployment in the manifest

the definition is a wf_schema_version 1 state machine: workflow_type, start_from, input_schema, initial_state, terminal_states, states with entry_actions, exit_actions and transitions (CEL guards), and an optional catch

a definition names in start_from the nodes whose messages start an instance: IO nodes or WFs, each a node name with its hive, never an AI.* node (an agent only answers) nor a SY.* or RT.* node; only the nodes written in it drive an instance
the person's IO node sends its messages to the WF: its config has io.dst_node: WF.<workflow_name>@<hive>
a WF asks an agent with a menu on a forward or a send_message to it; a known option such as answer is written by its name alone, and SY.wf-rules writes its description

an agent's answer to a forwarded message has no msg: match it by event_match.src; its text for the person, maybe empty, is event.context.evaluation.reply, and forwarding the answer to the person's IO node gives it to them
an agent's answers may arrive in any state (a person who writes twice gets two answers): the catch acts on them wherever they arrive
an agent's error answer is a payload of type 'error', with no retry: tell the person
every wait has a timer: a timeout is a TIMER_FIRED transition with the guard event.timer_key == '<timer_key>'
this is the basic loop; the handbook (§4.2) holds each other mechanism as a small case to combine: another agent, escalating a question or the conversation, a timer an answer sets, the catch
do_not_repeat: do not write a steps list: SY.wf-rules refuses any field its schema does not define
do not send messages to nodes that do not exist in the desired_state manifest or the system
do not write meta.type, target_ref, thread_id_ref, meta.context.response_envelope or event.payload.timer_key: SY.wf-rules refuses the first four, and the fifth is never set
do not put routing rules in an agent's role: the WF hands the agent a menu with each message, and the role keeps only the agent's trade
do not forward an agent's empty reply to an IO node: guard that forward with event.context.evaluation.reply != ''
do not ask an agent again with the same message: deliver its answer, then wait for the person's next message

trigger: Build an OPA Rego policy bundle for authorization or routing decisions.
constraints: rego_source must start with a 'package' declaration
package name must follow Rego naming convention (lowercase, dots as namespace separators)
the artifact must contain 'rego_source' as a top-level field
do_not_repeat: do not omit the 'package' declaration — it is required by OPA
do not embed raw JSON in Rego — use input.* references instead
do not use 'allow = true' as default — always default to false for security
